chunks: Those they invoke apart from Him have no power of intercession, except those who testify to the truth and have knowledge.
ai.seo_question: Who has the power of intercession according to this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse clarifies that intercession is not an inherent right of prophets or angels but is contingent upon divine permission and the individual's adherence to the 'Truth' (al-Haqq), often interpreted as Imam Ali or the Ahl al-Bayt. It refutes the idolaters' assumption that their deities can intercede independently, emphasizing that true intercession requires both testimony to monotheism and divine knowledge, thereby linking spiritual authority directly to the recognition of the rightful guides.
